claims.claim: re-aeration follows the lake-size wind model k600 = 2.51 + 1.48U + 0.39U·log10A cm/h (A in km², U the wind at 10 m)
claims.note: the equation is not in the abstract. The abstract's two worked values fit it exactly (reader's arithmetic: U = 5 m/s gives 6.0 cm/h at 1 ha and 13.8 cm/h at 100 km², against the abstract's '6 cm·h−1 in a small 1 ha lake to over 13 cm·h−1 in a 100 km2 system'), and it explains '68%' of the variance. The stand-in thesis (2010) has the same form with different coefficients: k600 = 2.48 (±1.05) + 1.45 (±0.30) U10 + 0.35 (±0.06) U10·log10 LA, r² = 0.67, n = 64 (PDF p. 70, printed 59, eq. 2.7, read on the page image) — so the published 2.51/1.48/0.39 must come from the article itself and cannot be confirmed from the thesis.

claims.claim: a cross-lake model gives about 1.6 m d⁻¹ for the 2.8–3.6-km² Hot Brook lakes at a 2.5 m s⁻¹ wind and 3.2 m d⁻¹ at 6.5 m s⁻¹ (project computation)
claims.note: the arithmetic holds on the equation as the paper gives it: U 2.5 → 6.65–6.75 cm/h = 1.60–1.62 m/d; U 6.5 → 13.3–13.5 cm/h = 3.18–3.25 m/d for A 2.8–3.6 km² (reader's arithmetic). The thesis's 2010 coefficients give almost the same (1.56 and 3.10 m/d at 2.8 km²). The input equation is unconfirmed until the article is read.

claims.claim: 1.6–4.7 m/day at 2.5–10 m/s for the real lakes' areas
claims.note: U 10 m/s, A 3.6 km²: 2.51 + 14.8 + 0.39·10·0.556 = 19.5 cm/h = 4.67 m/d (reader's arithmetic on the quoted equation); unconfirmed input.

notes: Stand-in: Vachon, D. 2010. 'Vitesse d'échange gazeux à l'interface air-eau : étude méthodologique et facteurs influents'. M.Sc. thesis, Université du Québec à Montréal (directed by Y. Prairie); https://archipel.uqam.ca/3549. Its chapter 2 (in English) fits k600 to wind and lake area on 64 floating-chamber measurements from the Eastmain-1 reservoir (602 km², James Bay) and 8 temperate lakes near Montreal (0.19–4.0 km², mean 1.36) — the same size range as the Hot Brook lakes — and gives model C (eq. 2.7, PDF p. 70): k600 = 2.48 + 1.45·U10 + 0.35·U10·log10(LA), r² = 0.67. It supports the model's form and its size range but not the 2013 coefficients; cite the article for those once read. The thesis's lake data are Quebec lakes much like Hot Brook, which helps the paper's caution (Klaus & Vachon 2020) about small lakes in light wind. The thesis is a scan with an OCR layer (its figure caption repeats the model with 0.34 for the interaction term; the equation itself reads 0.35 on the image).
